power: Refactor: Simplify dark resume logic. dark resume logic when written was expected to run on 3.8 kernel. 3.8 kernel did not have support for CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM and CLOCK_BOOTTIME_ALARM. As a result dark resume logic when need to sleep for certain time have to pound on /dev/rtc directly to schedule a wakeup. As we are not planning to run dark resume on older kernels, we can simply instantiate SimpleAlarmTimer in dark_resume.cc if needed. So let us not pass the suspend duration to suspender anymore. There is one more reason for this refactor. SimpleAlarmTimer in the backend use timerfd_* API. timerfd_* allow the kernel to manage a list of events and have it program the RTC so the alarm will trigger for the earliest event in the list. This avoids the need for user space applications to coordinate in order to share the hardware. For timerfd_* to work properly, no user daemon should touch /dev/rtc directly. But any suspend_duration passed to suspender will result in a write to /dev/rtc. So let us not do that.
